elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause opens "Upon expiration or any termination of this Agreement, SFJ shall ...", so both expiry and any termination trigger the obligations (curing the 14.2-only, no-Program-Transfer trigger in Section 14.3).

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: The insertion grants "reasonable transition assistance for at least ninety (90) days"; no six-month period appears anywhere. Section 14.3.4(ii)(y) states only "up to [***]", a redacted and therefore undefined period.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph is silent on pricing for the assistance; no "then-current rates" (or any rate basis) language is added, and retained 14.3.4 only allocates Clinical Trial continuation costs to PB.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination, deliver to PB all data generated in connection with the Clinical Trials, including the Trial Data Package and the Research Results included therein." The clock runs from expiry/termination, not from a request or from Product Filing assignment as in 14.3.3.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: No format specification is included in limb (b); the words "commonly used, machine-readable format" from the model language were not carried across, and no other retained provision imposes a format.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: The insertion contains no deletion or certification limb. Section 10.3 certifies destruction only of "Confidential Information" at the Disclosing Party's direction, is subject to survival/retention carve-outs, and is not sequenced after delivery of the trial data.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "Upon expiration or any termination of this Agreement" applies the assistance and delivery limbs to every covered exit event, unconditioned on the Section 14.2/Program Transfer gating in 14.3.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): SFJ shall "at PB's request, provide PB with reasonable transition assistance for at least ninety (90) days following such expiration or termination." The request condition is generic (mirrors model language) and is not tied only to anticipated expiry, so it does not defeat the element.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires delivery within 30 days of expiry/termination of "all data generated in connection with the Clinical Trials", the category of PB data held by SFJ under this Agreement; the named Trial Data Package/Research Results are inclusive examples, not a narrowing list.

reasons: Fallback is complete: the single inserted paragraph carries all three fallback elements in operative language — expiry-or-termination trigger, at least 90 days of assistance, and 30-day data delivery measured from the exit event rather than from a request or from Product Filing assignment.

Preferred is not complete: four elements are missing from the operative text — the six-month assistance period, the then-current-rates charging basis, the machine-readable format qualifier, and a post-return deletion-and-certification limb. To reach preferred, extend limb (a) to "up to six (6) months at SFJ's then-current rates", add "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" to limb (b), and add a limb (c) requiring deletion and written certification thereafter.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion into the termination section for a clause that is otherwise missing; Sections 14.3, 14.4 and 10.3 are left intact, no favourable language is deleted, and no extras (survival tail, expense allocation, procedures) are bolted on. The "including the Trial Data Package and the Research Results" phrase is borderline but is doing work here by anchoring the undefined generic "Customer Data" concept to this Agreement's defined data terms rather than merely illustrating a complete formula.

Intent preserved: 14.3's assignment/wind-down mechanics, cost allocations and the 10.3 Confidential Information return regime survive without contradiction; the new obligation is additive and its 30-day clock does not displace 14.3.3's separate Product Filings delivery. One drafting point to tighten: the new section is not added to the enumerated survival list in Section 14.4.3, so confirm it is either listed there or expressly stated to survive expiration and termination, to avoid an argument that the enumeration is exhaustive.

Classification as a deviation with an insert is correct: the pre-existing exit mechanics fail the fallback on material terms (14.3 does not operate on expiration or where a Program Transfer occurs, and both the assistance period and the delivery period are redacted, i.e. undefined triggers).
